public_payload.normalized_proposition: At least $300 billion of AI venture equity will be dead money because most AI startups are wrappers on Anthropic and OpenAI models.

statement.excerpt: Of those investments, I expect at least $300 billion of that equity to be dead money, because, for the most part, AI companies are wrappers or layers built on top of Anthropic and OpenAI’s models, holding very little IP of their own and being burdened with ever-growing opex that mostly flows to the two AI labs that constantly want to compete with their customers.

from_speaker: global venture capital investment in AI companies
at least $300 billion of that equity
wrappers or layers built on top of Anthropic and OpenAI’s models
our_interpretation: The investment cohort runs from January 2023 through the post date, September 29, 2026.
The ordinary reading of dead money is invested capital that ultimately produces no positive nominal return. This is not necessarily a forecast of $300 billion in outright losses.
Count invested principal, not headline company valuations. Temporary valuation reductions do not establish final investment returns.
The explanation about dependence on the labs requires separate evidence linking that dependence to poor returns.
criteria.support_condition: Final investment proceeds establish that at least $300 billion of principal in the specified cohort returned no more than its original investment. Evidence also links the predicted failure to the stated dependence on the labs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Complete final returns for the defined cohort establish that less than $300 billion of invested principal failed to earn a positive return. Successful individual investments alone cannot establish this.
